For a one-electron (hydrogen-like) species the Bohr energy is \(E_{n}=-2.18	imes10^{-18}\,\dfrac{Z^{2}}{n^{2}}\) J, and it is always NEGATIVE because the electron is bound.

(A) H, \(Z=1,n=2\): \(E=-2.18	imes10^{-18}/4=-5.45	imes10^{-19}\) J, not \(-1.09	imes10^{-18}\) J. False.
(B) \(He^{+}\), \(Z=2,n=2\): \(E=-2.18	imes10^{-18}	imes4/4=-2.18	imes10^{-18}\) J. The magnitude is right but the sign is positive in the option. False.
(C) \(He^{+}\), \(Z=2,n=1\): \(E=-2.18	imes10^{-18}	imes4/1=-8.72	imes10^{-18}\) J; again the option carries a positive sign. False.
(D) \(Li^{2+}\), \(Z=3,n=3\): \(E=-2.18	imes10^{-18}	imes9/9=-2.18	imes10^{-18}\) J. This matches exactly.

Hence (D) is the true statement.

Acetone is strongly self-associated through dipole-dipole interaction; adding \(CS_{2}\) breaks those acetone-acetone interactions and the new acetone-\(CS_{2}\) interactions are WEAKER. Escaping tendency therefore rises, so the mixture shows a POSITIVE deviation from Raoult's law.

For the partial pressure of \(CS_{2}\) this means \(p_{CS_{2}}>x_{CS_{2}}p^{\circ}_{CS_{2}}\) at every intermediate composition: the curve must start at the origin, bow ABOVE the straight Raoult line, and meet \(p^{\circ}_{CS_{2}}\) at \(x_{CS_{2}}=1\) where it becomes tangent to that line. In the very dilute region it instead follows the steeper Henry's law tangent.

Graph (A) is the only one showing a single \(p_{CS_{2}}\) curve lying between the Raoult line (below) and the Henry line (above). (C) is the ideal straight-line case, (B) bows below the ideal lines (negative deviation), and (D) plots the whole set of partial and total pressures rather than the partial pressure of \(CS_{2}\) asked for. Hence (A).

First ionization enthalpies across period 3 (kJ mol\(^{-1}\)): Al 577, Si 786, P 1012, S 1000, Cl 1251.

Two irregularities control the order. Al is lower than Mg because its electron leaves a \(3p\) orbital rather than a filled \(3s\); and S is lower than P because P has the extra-stable half-filled \(3p^{3}\) configuration whereas removing an electron from \(3p^{4}\) in S relieves inter-electronic repulsion in the doubly occupied \(p\) orbital.

Therefore \(Al<Si<S<P<Cl\), which is option (A).

In \(Ag(s)|AgCl(s)|FeCl_{2},FeCl_{3}|Pt(s)\) the left electrode is the anode and the right the cathode.

Anode: \(Ag+Cl^{-}ightarrow AgCl+e^{-}\)
Cathode: \(Fe^{3+}+e^{-}ightarrow Fe^{2+}\)
Net: \(Ag+Cl^{-}+Fe^{3+}ightarrow AgCl+Fe^{2+}\)

Nernst equation (\(n=1\)): \(E_{cell}=E^{\circ}_{cell}-0.059\,\log\dfrac{[Fe^{2+}]}{[Cl^{-}][Fe^{3+}]}\).

\(E_{cell}\) rises whenever the reaction quotient falls, i.e. when \([Fe^{2+}]\) is DECREASED, or \([Fe^{3+}]\) is INCREASED, or \([Cl^{-}]\) is INCREASED. Those are statements C, D and E; increasing \([Fe^{2+}]\) (A) or decreasing \([Fe^{3+}]\) (B) lowers the cell potential.

Hence the correct choice is C, D and E only, option (D).

Identify the two carbonyl partners.

\(x\): propanenitrile with \(SnCl_{2}/HCl\) followed by hydrolysis is the Stephen reaction, \(CH_{3}CH_{2}CNightarrow CH_{3}CH_{2}CHO\) (propanal).
\(y\): but-2-ene with \(O_{3}\) then hydrolysis gives two molecules of \(CH_{3}CHO\) (ethanal).

With alkali and heat the two aldehydes undergo aldol condensation. Both have alpha-hydrogens, so four crossed/self combinations are possible:
- propanal enolate + propanal \(ightarrow\) 2-methylpent-2-enal (option C).
- propanal enolate + ethanal \(ightarrow\) 2-methylbut-2-enal (option A).
- ethanal enolate + propanal \(ightarrow\) pent-2-enal (option B).
- ethanal enolate + ethanal \(ightarrow\) but-2-enal (not listed).

Molar mass of 4-nitrotoluene \(C_{7}H_{7}NO_{2}=137\) g mol\(^{-1}\), so 137 mg is exactly 1 mmol.

Step 1: \(Sn/HCl\) then neutralisation reduces \(-NO_{2}\) to \(-NH_{2}\), giving A = 4-methylaniline.
Step 2(i): acetic anhydride acetylates the amine to 4-methylacetanilide, \(C_{9}H_{11}NO\) (M = 149).
Step 2(ii): \(Br_{2}/AcOH\) brominates the ring. The \(-NHCOCH_{3}\) group is the stronger activating ortho/para director and its para position is blocked by \(-CH_{3}\), so bromination occurs ORTHO to the acetamido group. B = 2-bromo-4-methylacetanilide, \(C_{9}H_{10}BrNO\).

M(B) \(=149-1+80=228\) g mol\(^{-1}\). One mmol therefore gives 228 mg, option (C).

(The acetylation step is used precisely to moderate the strongly activating \(-NH_{2}\) so that only mono-bromination occurs.)

The microwave delivers energy to the water, so heat flows INTO the system: \(q>0\).

Once the water boils it turns to steam, and the vapour expands against the surrounding atmosphere. The system does work on the surroundings, so with the convention \(w=-p_{ext}\Delta V\) and \(\Delta V>0\) we get \(w<0\).

By the first law \(\Delta U=q+w\). The heat supplied must raise the temperature from \(5^{\circ}C\) to \(100^{\circ}C\) AND supply the large enthalpy of vaporisation, so \(|q|\gg|w|\) and \(\Delta U>0\).

Hence \(q=+ve,\ w=-ve,\ \Delta U=+ve\), option (B).

The relevant part of the spectrochemical series is \(I^{-}<Br^{-}<Cl^{-}<F^{-}<H_{2}O<NH_{3}<CN^{-}\); field strength, and hence the d-orbital splitting, increases from left to right.

Statement I: \(Br^{-}\) is a weaker field ligand than \(Cl^{-}\), so \(\Delta_{t}[CoBr_{4}]^{2-}<\Delta_{t}[CoCl_{4}]^{2-}\). A smaller splitting means a smaller \(\Delta E\) for the d-d transition, so light of LOWER energy (longer wavelength) is absorbed. Statement I is TRUE.

Statement II: \(I^{-}\) is weaker still than \(Cl^{-}\), so \(\Delta_{t}[CoI_{4}]^{2-}<\Delta_{t}[CoCl_{4}]^{2-}\) - the separation is LESS, not more. Statement II is FALSE.

Hence option (B).

One mole of \(H_{2}\) on but-2-yne gives partial reduction. Syn (cis) delivery of hydrogen from the metal surface with \(Pd/C\) gives X = cis-but-2-ene; dissolving-metal reduction with \(Na/\) liquid \(NH_{3}\) proceeds through a trans-vinyl anion and gives Y = trans-but-2-ene.

(A) cis- and trans-but-2-ene differ only in spatial arrangement about the C=C, so they ARE stereoisomers (geometrical isomers). Correct statement.
(B) X is the CIS isomer; the two \(C-CH_{3}\) bond dipoles do not cancel, so its dipole moment is NOT zero (it is the trans isomer that has zero dipole moment). INCORRECT.
(C) The polar cis isomer has stronger dipole-dipole attraction and hence the higher boiling point (cis 3.7 \(^{\circ}C\), trans 0.9 \(^{\circ}C\)). Correct statement.
(D) Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C in both, and both give two molecules of \(CH_{3}CHO\) - the SAME products. INCORRECT.

The incorrect statements are B and D, option (B).

From the figure A = chlorobenzene, B = nitrobenzene, C = anisole (methoxybenzene). Nitration is an electrophilic aromatic substitution, so reactivity tracks the electron density the substituent puts on the ring.

- B (\(-NO_{2}\)): strongly electron-withdrawing by both \(-I\) and \(-R\); powerfully deactivating. Nitrobenzene needs far harsher conditions than benzene.
- A (\(-Cl\)): the \(-I\) effect outweighs the weak \(+R\) donation, so chlorobenzene is mildly deactivated, but far more reactive than nitrobenzene.
- C (\(-OCH_{3}\)): strong \(+R\) donation from the oxygen lone pair outweighs its \(-I\); anisole is strongly ACTIVATED and the most reactive.

Increasing order of reactivity: \(B<A<C\), option (D).

(A) It is the well known bright RED precipitate. Correct statement.

Tollens' reagent oxidises only REDUCING sugars, i.e. those whose cyclic form is a hemiacetal (free \(-OH\) on the anomeric carbon) and can therefore ring-open to a free aldehyde in solution. A glycoside, in which the anomeric \(-OH\) has been replaced by \(-OCH_{3}\), is a full ACETAL: it cannot open in neutral or basic medium and is non-reducing.

Reading the four structures:
(A) pyranose with a free \(-OH\) on the anomeric carbon (next to the ring oxygen) - hemiacetal, REDUCES Tollens'.
(B) pyranose bearing \(-OCH_{3}\) on the anomeric carbon - methyl glycoside, does NOT react.
(C) furanose bearing \(-OCH_{3}\) on the anomeric carbon - methyl glycoside, does NOT react.
(D) pyranose with a free anomeric \(-OH\) - hemiacetal, REDUCES Tollens'.

So B and C fail to react, option (D).

Count lone pairs from each Lewis structure (total valence electrons minus bonding electrons, divided by 2).

\(HNO_{3}\): 24 valence electrons, 5 bonds (10 e) used, leaving 14 e = 7 lone pairs.
\(H_{2}SO_{4}\): 32 valence electrons, 8 bonds (16 e), leaving 16 e = 8 lone pairs.
\(NF_{3}\): 26 valence electrons, 3 bonds (6 e), leaving 20 e = 10 lone pairs (one on N, three on each F).
\(O_{3}\): 18 valence electrons, 3 bonds (6 e), leaving 12 e = 6 lone pairs.

So \(X=NF_{3}\) with 10 lone pairs.

\(NF_{3}\) has four electron domains about nitrogen (three bond pairs, one lone pair), so it is pyramidal. The lone pair compresses the angle below the tetrahedral \(109.5^{\circ}\), and the high electronegativity of fluorine pulls the bond pairs away from N, compressing it further than in \(NH_{3}\) (\(107^{\circ}\)). The observed \(F-N-F\) angle is about \(102^{\circ}\), option (C).

Statement-I: The criterion for sublimation is that the SOLID passes directly into the vapour state on heating without melting, i.e. it has an appreciable vapour pressure below its melting point. Sublimation separates such sublimable solids (camphor, naphthalene, benzoic acid, anthracene) from non-sublimable impurities. A merely low melting point is neither the criterion nor a guarantee - a low-melting solid usually just melts. Statement-I is FALSE.

Statement-II: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure. Reducing the external pressure means a lower vapour pressure suffices, so the boiling point DECREASES - this is exactly why heat-sensitive liquids are distilled under reduced pressure. Statement-II is FALSE.

Both statements are false, option (D).

Work backwards from the product, cyclohexyl isocyanide.

The last step, \(CHCl_{3}+\) alcoholic \(KOH\), heat, is the carbylamine (isocyanide) test, which works only on a PRIMARY amine. So the amine entering that step is cyclohexylamine, \(C_{6}H_{11}NH_{2}\).

The step before it, \(Br_{2}/KOH\), is Hofmann bromamide degradation, which converts a primary amide \(RCONH_{2}\) into \(RNH_{2}\) with LOSS of one carbon. To deliver \(C_{6}H_{11}NH_{2}\), Q must be cyclohexanecarboxamide, \(C_{6}H_{11}CONH_{2}\).

Finally, P with \(NH_{3}\) then heat gives an amide: the acid first forms its ammonium salt, which loses water on heating. Hence P = cyclohexanecarboxylic acid, \(C_{6}H_{11}COOH\).

Comparing with the structures drawn, that is option (B). Option (A) is cyclohexylacetaldehyde, (C) is 1-cyclohexylpropan-1-one and (D) is the amide Q itself, which would not need the ammonia step.

Start with 1 mol \(NH_{3}\) and let the degree of dissociation be \(\alpha\).

\(NH_{3}:1-\alpha\), \(N_{2}:\alpha/2\), \(H_{2}:3\alpha/2\); total moles \(=1+\alpha\).

With total pressure \(P\),
\(p_{NH_{3}}=\dfrac{(1-\alpha)P}{1+\alpha}\), \(p_{N_{2}}=\dfrac{\alpha P}{2(1+\alpha)}\), \(p_{H_{2}}=\dfrac{3\alpha P}{2(1+\alpha)}\).

\(K_{p}=\dfrac{p_{N_{2}}^{1/2}p_{H_{2}}^{3/2}}{p_{NH_{3}}}\). Collecting powers of \(P\) gives \(P^{1/2+3/2-1}=P\), and the numerical factors give \(3^{3/2}/2^{2}\) times \(\alpha^{2}/(1+\alpha)^{2}\), so

\(K_{p}=\dfrac{3^{3/2}}{4}\cdot\dfrac{\alpha^{2}P}{1-\alpha^{2}}\).

Put \(P=\sqrt{3}\): \(3^{3/2}\sqrt{3}=3^{2}=9\), so \(K_{p}=\dfrac{9\alpha^{2}}{4(1-\alpha^{2})}\).

Setting \(K_{p}=9\): \(\alpha^{2}=4(1-\alpha^{2})\Rightarrow 5\alpha^{2}=4\Rightarrow\alpha^{2}=0.8\).

Given \(\alpha=(x	imes10^{-2})^{-1/2}\), squaring gives \(\alpha^{2}=\dfrac{1}{x	imes10^{-2}}\), so \(x=\dfrac{100}{\alpha^{2}}=\dfrac{100}{0.8}=125\).

Hence \(x=125\).
